finalists.label: Bardet-Biedl syndrome
finalists.why: It has strong for evidence including high bilateral myopia, truncal obesity, and joint hyperextensibility, with only one against entry that is not decisive.

finalists.label: Syndromic disorder
finalists.why: It accounts for multiple findings including severe rod–cone retinal dystrophy, high bilateral myopia, moderate intellectual disability, and transient neutropenia in childhood.

finalists.label: Warburg Micro Syndrome
finalists.why: It explains moderate intellectual disability and microcephaly, despite having one against entry for high bilateral myopia.

frontier_selector.why: Bardet-Biedl syndrome is chosen because it specifically accounts for the patient's high bilateral myopia, truncal obesity, and joint hyperextensibility, which are distinctive features of the syndrome.
